Glossary.label: Glossary
Glossary.title: 3D file formats and terms, explained
Glossary.subtitle: Quick definitions for the words you'll meet when you export a model.

stl.def: Stores a 3D shape as a list of triangles. The standard file you load into a 3D printer slicer like Cura, PrusaSlicer or Bambu Studio.

glb.def: A single binary glTF 2.0 file with geometry, materials and textures inside. Unity, Unreal, Godot and most web viewers read it natively.

obj.def: The classic mesh format read by Blender, Maya and Cinema 4D. Carries geometry and UVs, and pairs with an MTL for materials.

fbx.def: Autodesk's legacy interchange format. Older Unity projects and some studio pipelines still rely on it for animated meshes.

gltf.def: An open Khronos standard for 3D scenes. GLB is the binary, single-file flavor of glTF.

watertight.def: A mesh with no holes or gaps. 3D printer slicers need this to compute layers cleanly.

pbr.def: Physically based rendering uses albedo, normal and roughness maps so a surface stays consistent under any light.

mesh.def: The surface of a 3D object made of vertices, edges and faces. Every Bunshin export is a mesh.

3d-printing.section1Title: Watertight STL Files, Ready to Slice
3d-printing.section1Text: One of the biggest frustrations in 3D printing is receiving a model with holes, non-manifold edges, or inverted normals that fails in your slicer. Bunshin 3D generates watertight, manifold meshes by design. The STL files load directly into popular slicers like Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio, and Simplify3D without requiring mesh repair tools. Whether you are printing on FDM, SLA, or SLS printers, the geometry is solid and ready to slice.
3d-printing.section2Text: Turn a child's drawing into a figurine, convert a company logo into a desk trophy, or transform a product sketch into a prototype. The AI analyzes your image and reconstructs full 3D geometry with depth, curves, and surface detail. not just flat extrusions or lithophanes. The result is a genuinely three-dimensional model that looks great from every angle when printed.
3d-printing.section3Text: You do not need to learn Blender, ZBrush, or any CAD software. Upload your image, wait about 30 seconds, and download your STL. The entire process happens in your browser. This makes 3D printing accessible to hobbyists, educators, small business owners, and anyone who has an image they want to hold in their hands.
3d-printing.faq1Q: Are the STL files truly print-ready?
3d-printing.faq1A: Yes. All STL exports are watertight and manifold. They load directly into slicers like Cura, PrusaSlicer, and Bambu Studio without needing repair in Meshmixer or Netfabb.
3d-printing.faq2Q: What types of images work best for 3D printing?
3d-printing.faq2A: Clear images with a single subject on a plain background produce the best results. Logos, product photos, character illustrations, and simple drawings all work well. Avoid busy backgrounds or multiple overlapping objects.
3d-printing.faq3Q: Can I scale the model before printing?
3d-printing.faq3A: Yes. The STL file can be scaled freely in your slicer software. The mesh geometry is resolution-independent, so you can scale up or down without losing structural integrity.
3d-printing.faq4Q: Does it work with resin printers (SLA)?
3d-printing.faq4A: Yes. The watertight STL files are compatible with both FDM and SLA/resin printers. The solid mesh structure ensures clean slicing regardless of your printer type.
